0313.name: OAM properties, tile 68
desc: Properties byte (YXPPCCCT: flips, priority, palette, name table bit) of OAM entry 68, the fifth entry of the
$0300 page. Draw routines index it with Y: checkerboard platform, turn block bridge, bonus game block, Mario's
cape/draw tables each store the tile's properties here; the Fishin' Boo graphics flips it with EOR.

0340.name: OAM X position, entry 80
desc: Byte 0 (the X position) of OAM entry 80, the first entry of the $0340 block in the shadow OAM buffer.
Written with STA,Y by the three-tile rope column sprite and the switch palace ! block particles: screen X
low byte.
Copied to the PPU by the NMI OAM DMA.

Copied to the PPU by the NMI OAM DMA.

0343.name: OAM properties, entry 80

0400.name: OAM high table, sprites 0-3
desc: First byte of the packed OAM high table: 2 bits per sprite (X bit 8 and size) for sprites 0-3.
Built each frame from the one-byte-per-sprite entries at $0420-$049F by the 'Pack OAM size bits' routine,
which ORs $0420,$0421,$0422,$0423 together shifted two bits apart. Game mode 00 and the switch icon code write
it directly (e.g. $AA = all four sprites 16x16).
Bits: 0-1 sprite 0, 2-3 sprite 1, 4-5 sprite 2, 6-7 sprite 3 (each: bit 0 = X bit 8, bit 1 = large size).

0420.name: OAM size bits, sprite 0
0420.kind: byte, one per OAM sprite (indexed by X or Y)
desc: Per-sprite size/X-high entry for OAM sprite 0 (OAM entry at $0200); the NMI-bound packed table is $0400-$041F.
Draw routines store a value here after writing the tile; the packer folds four of these into one $0400 byte.
Heavily used (about 60 sites): extended, minor extended, score, smoke and bounce sprites all write it.
Values: 0 = 8x8 on-screen, 2 = 16x16, 3 = 16x16 with X bit 8 set (sprite on the next page).

Draw routines store a value here after writing the tile; the packer folds four of these into one $0400 byte.

desc: Per-sprite size/X-high entry for OAM sprite 40 (OAM entry at $02A0); the NMI-bound packed table is

Values: 0 = 8x8 on-screen, 2 = 16x16, 3 = 16x16 with X bit 8 set (sprite on the next page).

0460.kind: byte, one per OAM sprite (indexed by X or Y)

desc: Per-sprite size/X-high entry for OAM sprite 96 (OAM entry at $0380); the NMI-bound packed table is

04A0.name: Window HDMA table, left edge
04A0.kind: byte table, 2 bytes per scanline (left, right)
desc: Window left edge per scanline for the HDMA windowing effect on channel 7 (to $2126). The table has 224
lines of
2 bytes: $04A0 + 2*line is the left edge and $04A1 + 2*line is the right edge (WH0/WH1); lines 0-111 are here
and lines 112-223 continue at $0580. An empty window is left $FF / right $00 (or left 1).
Written by iris-out/peace pose, dark room spotlight, screen wipes, overworld load and the lives exchange.

04A1.name: Window HDMA table, right edge
04A1.kind: byte table, 2 bytes per scanline (left, right)
desc: Window right edge per scanline, interleaved with $04A0 (left edge) in the channel 7 HDMA window table.
Right $FF with left $00 covers the whole line; left $FF with right $00 is empty. Cleared and filled by the
HDMA window init at $00:9263 and by the iris/spotlight routines (peace pose, dark room, overworld load).

0590.name: Window table, line 112 area
0590.kind: byte table (ROM bytes mixed in), shares $04A0 HDMA table
desc: In RAM, part of the second half of the windowing HDMA table at $0580 (lines 112-223, left/right pairs).
The lives exchange iris effect stores the window edge here ($0590,X) and at $0548,Y for the upper half.
The 9 read hits are not RAM: the layer 3 image table in bank 05 contains bytes that look like $0590.

0680.name: Palette upload select
0680.kind: byte (0, 3 or 6); doubles as ROM pointer bytes
desc: Requests a CGRAM palette upload in NMI and selects which buffer: 0 = none/queue at $0682, 3 = list at $0905,
6 = list at $0703. The upload routine ('MoreDMA') clears it to 0 once the records are sent; the level-end
dithered fade and the overworld submap/event code set 3 or 6; the finish pose code checks for 3.
Most of the 284 hits are not RAM: the level layer 1 data pointer table in bank 05 holds $06:8000-style
addresses.

0681.name: Palette queue write index
desc: Offset of the end of the queued CGRAM record list at $0682 (the first free byte). Magikoopa, Big Boo,
Peach ending fade, Bowser room lightning and overworld sprites read it, append a record at $0682+index and
advance it. Cleared with the RAM clear and when the upload (option 0) completes.

0682.name: Palette queue first byte count
desc: First byte of the queued palette upload list: each record is [byte count][CGRAM start index][color data],
with a count of 0 ending the list. Written (count $10 = 8 colors, 2 = one color) by Magikoopa, Big Boo,
Peach and
Bowser room code, indexed by X/Y from $0681; cleared by the uploader when empty.
Some hits are ROM pointer bytes in the bank 05 level layer 1 data table.

0683.name: Palette queue CGRAM index
desc: Second byte of a queued palette record: the CGRAM color index where the colors go. $F0 = last sprite palette,
$F1 = a single color, 0 = backdrop, $47 and $02 are other overworld/cutscene targets. Written by Magikoopa,
Big Boo, Peach fade, Bowser room, overworld sprites and the cutscene phase palette loader.

0684.name: Palette queue color data (low)
desc: First data byte of a queued palette record (color low byte of the first color; the record continues at $0685,
$0686...). Written by Bowser room lightning, scene phase palette, Magikoopa, Big Boo, Peach and overworld
sprites
through X/Y index from $0681.

0685.name: Palette queue color high byte
desc: Second data byte of a queued palette record: the high byte of the first color (with $0684 as the low byte).
Bowser room lightning zeroes it as the default color 0 before replacing it.
Some read hits are ROM pointer bytes in the bank 05 level layer 1 data table.

0686.name: Palette queue data / end marker
desc: Third data byte of a queued palette record (color 1 low byte); Bowser room lightning writes colors 1-7 here.
Peach and overworld sprites write 0 at this position (+X) as the end-of-list terminator.
Most of the 33 hits are not RAM: bank 05 level layer 1/2 data pointer tables hold these bytes.

0691.name: Palette queue second record CGRAM index
desc: In the cutscene scene phase palette load, the second queued palette record is placed at $0690: count $0C at
$0690 and CGRAM index $12 at $0691. In RAM it is just the second byte of whichever record starts at $0690.
One hit is a ROM pointer byte in the bank 05 level layer 1 data table (level $015).

0694.name: Palette queue terminator
desc: A zero here ends the queued CGRAM record list after one record (record size 2 + $10 data bytes from $0682
Magikoopa and the Big Boo boss store 0 here with STZ,X to terminate the queue.
One hit is a ROM pointer byte in the bank 05 level layer 1 data table (level $0E3).
